recent_posts.title: Using Project Aristotle To Build Highly Effective Teams
recent_posts.summary: Google's Project Aristotle identified five key factors for building highly effective teams: psychological safety, dependability, structure and clarity, meaning, and impact. Leaders can enhance these factors through various activities and assessments, ensuring continuous adaptation to maintain team effectiveness. Misinterpretations and neglecting individual contributions or leadership investment can undermine these efforts.

recent_posts.title: Results from Work Mode Survey
recent_posts.summary: A recent survey of over 100 respondents revealed that the majority prefer hybrid working arrangements (68%), followed by fully remote work (31%). Very few (1%) are working full-time in an office. Most respondents who go to the office spend 1-3 days per week there, with a significant number (34%) spending 3 or more days. The results indicate that the hybrid/remote work trend is prevalent and likely to continue.

recent_posts.title: The Trident Model of Career Development
recent_posts.summary: Tech companies often use growth frameworks or career ladders to define shared expectations for growth and promotion. However, career ladders have limitations and can be treated as checklists. The Trident Career Model offers three tracks for career development: the Management Track, the Technical Leadership Track, and the True Individual Contributor Track.

recent_posts.title: Patterns Mean Progress
recent_posts.summary: The book Diffusion of Innovation says innovation goes through several successive groups – Innovators (Risk Takers), Early Adopters (Opinion Leaders), Early Majority, Late Majority (Skeptics) and the Laggards (Last to Try) As innovation (or tech) moves between stages, you might notice specific signals.
